clue.text: Ways of viewing misuse of space on back-street

indicators.note: misusing the letters of the word means jumbling them into a new order
back, attached to the street, says its abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Ways of looking at the poor use of room behind a side road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse of' rearranges SPACE into ASPEC; 'back' in 'back-street' turns ST round to TS, which is put on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspects are the angles or sides from which a matter can be regarded.

clue.text: An artist set up secure high-level lighting

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the piece is written upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
to clamp something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: A painter rigs firmly fastened overhead lamps for a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RA into AR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc-lamp is a bright electric light, often mounted high, as in floodlighting or old cinema projection.

clue.text: All long for self-assurance

parts.note: pan- is the Greek prefix meaning all, as in pandemic
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Everyone yearns to feel confident.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style or manner.

clue.text: Feature a dinner-service?

parts.note: the chin is one of the features of the face

explanation.surface: Asks whether a set of plates counts as a highlight of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' looks like a verb or a newspaper item but is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, and a set of it for a meal is a dinner service.

clue.text: This always ran to time

parts.note: a timer whose fine grains flow from one bulb to another, so it was literally 'running' and always kept the set interval

explanation.surface: Something that was never late.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandglass is an hourglass: sand running through a narrow neck measures a fixed period.

clue.text: Boxes with some hesitation, being comparatively thin

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A boxer fights tentatively and is rather skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparser is the comparative of sparse, meaning more thinly spread.

clue.text: Wrap for a writer over 50

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A garment for an author past fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a piece of cloth worn draped around the shoulders, a wrap.

clue.text: Rendering odd items in musical form would be a bloomer

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the musical piece

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: odd describes the letters of items as strangely arranged

explanation.surface: Turning strange objects into song would be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ITEMS into TEMIS, which goes 'in' ARIA. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of plants including wormwood and mugwort, so it is something that flowers.

clue.text: Women who are highly vocal!

parts.note: not loud-mouthed women but singers whose voices sit at the top of the range, in the Italian plural

explanation.surface: Women who make a lot of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural for singers of the highest female voice.

clue.text: No Tory's represented this town

indicators.note: re-presented, so the letters are presented again in a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: No Conservative has ever been the MP for this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges NO TORYS. ROYSTON is a market town in Hertfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Royston is an English town on the Hertfordshire-Cambridgeshire border.

clue.text: Poles in a corner arranging transfer

indicators.note: in places the poles inside the corner

parts.note: a coign is a projecting corner of a building
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Putting tent poles in a corner while organising a move.
explanation.walkthrough: COIGN, an old word for a corner stone, is less familiar than its cousin 'quoin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to send them or hand them over for delivery.

clue.text: A spy out to make personal investigation

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agent goes out to do some snooping himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges A SPY OUT. The definition reflects the Greek root: seeing for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy, from Greek for seeing with one's own eyes, is a first-hand examination, usually of a body.

clue.text: Taking a right turn left port

parts.note: a turn, as in a turn of events, is a change

explanation.surface: A driver turns right and leaves the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the left side of a ship next to 'left', but it is the definition: a port city.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian seaport on the White Sea.

clue.text: Some may soon become antiquated, it's implied

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some things will soon be outdated, it's suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: What was meant was intended or suggested rather than said outright.

clue.text: Newspaper drive?

explanation.definitionFit: The press means journalism and newspapers; to press is to push hard, to drive.

clue.text: Give voice about the answer that's offensive

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
in crosswords an answer entered in the grid is called a light

explanation.surface: Speak up about the reply that caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SING round LIGHT, the crossword term for a grid answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighting remarks are disparaging, insulting ones.

clue.text: A large number charge for making introduction

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a mission is a task one is charged with

explanation.surface: Many pay a fee to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is entry or being let in, an introduction into a place or group.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink provided only after some agitation

definitions.text: Non-alcoholic drink provided only after some agitation

parts.words: Non-alcoholic drink provided only after some agitation
parts.note: a dairy drink that is not ready until it has been shaken vigorously

explanation.surface: A soft drink you only get after making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is cold milk blended or shaken with flavouring.

clue.text: Southern girl dressed in laid-back sacking

indicators.note: dressed in means the pieces are put inside the other, as if clothed by it
back, joined to laid, says those letters run the other way

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl from the south, dressed casually, gets fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' in 'laid-back' turns LAID into DIAL; 'dressed in' puts S and MISS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is dismissal from a job.

clue.text: It's taken a mother years to get compensation

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse
ages means a very long time, years

explanation.surface: It took a mum years to be paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money awarded by a court to make up for loss or injury.

clue.text: Satisfy about blunder and make certain cuts

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy fully
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Fill up after a mistake and make some cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To serrate is to give an edge a row of tooth-like notches.

clue.text: A special dish for sanctimonious Conservative leader

parts.note: as can mean for, as in 'as a reward'
pi is short for pious, sanctimonious

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A party chef cooks for a self-righteous Tory boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' giving AS is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly in which meat or fish is set, a dish in its own right.

clue.text: Individual-a man of rank

definitions.meaning: a soldier in the ranks, the lowest grade

explanation.definitionFit: Private means personal to one person; a private is a soldier of the lowest rank who serves in the ranks.

clue.text: Be about one's business

definitions.meaning: to relate to or have as subject

explanation.definitionFit: To concern is to relate to; a concern is a business or firm, and also one's affair.

clue.text: Given a month to move on

definitions.meaning: the third month of the year

explanation.definitionFit: March is the third month of the calendar and also means to walk steadily forward in step.

clue.text: A Spaniard seeing about Italians' accommodation

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: accommodating the letters means fitting them into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man from Spain sees to housing for some Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' rearranges ITALIANS into ASTILIAN after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A Castilian is a native of Castile, the central region of Spain.

clue.text: The mating game

parts.note: not courtship but a board game won by checkmating the opponent's king

explanation.surface: The business of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is won by checkmate, so it is literally a game of mating.

clue.text: Plans changes in a side

indicators.note: changes says the letters of a side are reordered

explanation.surface: A team makes changes to its strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are schemes or plans for doing something.

clue.text: Jar with nickel interior for the hard stuff

indicators.note: interior means the metal sits inside the other word

parts.note: to jar is to grate on the nerves
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A jar with a metal lining for strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' suggests spirits; it is a very hard rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous rock.

clue.text: Having to state one's date of birth is normal

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state
one's date of birth fixes one's age

explanation.surface: Having to give your birth date is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or ordinary.

clue.text: Destroys sound vehicles that skid

indicators.note: sound says the word is said out loud and matched to another spelling

parts.note: slays means kills or destroys

explanation.surface: Wrecks solid cars that slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (solid) but is the homophone signal; sledges skid along snow on runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleighs are sledges that slide over snow on runners.

clue.text: Unusual sea fowl-oriental

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of sea are in an odd order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A strange seabird from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means of the East, oriental.
